settings.heading: Psychological Evaluations
settings.subheading: Comprehensive assessment for children, adolescents, and adults. Diagnostic clarity that informs treatment, supports school and workplace accommodations, and helps you understand yourself more fully.

settings.heading: Not a checkbox exercise. A clinical process.
settings.body:
Psychological evaluation at Center for Balanced Living is a thorough, individualized process. We integrate clinical interview, record review, behavioral observation, and psychometric testing to produce findings that are accurate, actionable, and clearly communicated.

Every evaluation concludes with a written report and a dedicated feedback session, where results are explained in plain language and next steps are discussed. We do not simply deliver scores. We help you understand what they mean.

Evaluations are conducted by Dr. Angela Serravalle, a licensed psychologist with advanced training in psychometric assessment and trauma-based practice.

settings.heading: Types of Evaluation
settings.subheading: We conduct evaluations across a range of clinical questions.

settings.title: Autism Spectrum Evaluation
settings.description: Comprehensive assessment for children, adolescents, and adults where autism spectrum disorder is a clinical question. Includes ADOS-2, ADI-R (when indicated), cognitive testing, and adaptive functioning measures.

settings.title: ADHD and Executive Function
settings.description: Assessment of attention, working memory, processing speed, and executive functioning for children, adolescents, and adults. Supports diagnosis, accommodation requests, and treatment planning.

settings.title: Academic and Learning Concerns
settings.description: Evaluation for learning disabilities, reading disorders, processing differences, and academic underachievement. Commonly requested for IEP, 504 Plan, and college accommodation documentation.

settings.title: Personality and Emotional Functioning
settings.description: Assessment of personality structure, emotional regulation, relational patterns, and diagnostic questions related to mood, anxiety, trauma, and personality. Often requested when clinical picture is complex or unclear.

settings.title: Diagnostic Clarification
settings.description: Targeted assessment when an existing diagnosis is in question, when multiple diagnoses are present, or when prior testing was inconclusive. Helps refine treatment direction and supports second opinions.

settings.heading: What to expect, from intake to feedback.
settings.body:
Intake consultation. We begin with a clinical interview to understand your referral question, history, and goals for the evaluation.

Testing sessions. Depending on the evaluation type, testing may take place over one or more sessions, typically 2 to 4 hours each. We pace testing to optimize performance and comfort.

Scoring and report. We analyze results, integrate all data sources, and produce a written report that is clear, jargon-minimal, and clinically useful.

Feedback session. We review findings together, answer questions, and discuss recommendations. You will leave understanding what the results mean and what to do next.

settings.quote: The evaluation gave us language for what we had been seeing for years. The feedback session was the first time we actually understood what our child needed.

settings.question: How long does an evaluation take?
settings.answer: Most evaluations involve 2 to 4 hours of direct testing, distributed across one or two sessions. The full process from intake to feedback typically takes 4 to 8 weeks depending on scheduling and report turnaround.

settings.question: Does insurance cover psychological evaluations?
settings.answer: Coverage varies by plan and by the reason for evaluation. Evaluations conducted for diagnostic or clinical purposes are often covered. Evaluations requested solely for school or workplace documentation may not be. We recommend contacting your insurance provider before scheduling.

settings.question: Can you evaluate adults, or only children?
settings.answer: We evaluate children, adolescents, and adults. Many of our adult referrals involve questions about ADHD, autism, or complex diagnostic presentations that were not identified earlier in life.

settings.question: Will I receive a written report?
settings.answer: Yes. Every evaluation includes a written psychological report and a live feedback session. We do not release reports without a feedback meeting.

settings.question: Do you provide documentation for school accommodations or disability services?
settings.answer: Yes. Our reports are written to meet the documentation standards required by most school districts, colleges, and universities. We are familiar with IEP, 504 Plan, and disability services office requirements.
